attacks.claim: The GRT routing-layer adjustment of 0.45 is too aggressive for this design; the default 30 congestion iterations were also insufficient
attacks.problem: Thread never isolates the effect of the 0.45→0.2 change from the iteration-count change, nor supplies before/after overflow or congestion metrics. attacks.correct_version: Lowering layer adjustment to 0.2 together with raising congestion iterations to 35 allowed GRT to finish on the reporter’s instance; relative contribution of each change, and whether macro looping was the deeper cause, remains unproven.

attacks.claim: chosen_intervention: Per eder-matheus we could finish GRT by changing the routing layer adjustments from 0.45 to 0.2... We also changed the number of congestion iterations to 35 to complete BoomTile
attacks.problem: Quoted statement describes a local experiment, not a committed or upstreamed change. Draft’s own gaps already note absence of any PR and unknown merge status; elevating the quote to ‘chosen_intervention’ overstates status.
attacks.correct_version: Experimental parameter values (layer-adjustment 0.2 + congestion iterations 35) that permitted GRT to complete on one machine; no evidence the values were merged or became defaults.

attacks.claim: post_state: GRT was reported to complete after reducing the layer adjustment to 0.2 and setting congestion iterations to 35
attacks.problem: Only evidence is a single developer sentence. No post-change DRC count, overflow number, heatmap, runtime, or confirmation that detailed routing subsequently succeeded appears in the record. Auto-closure as not_planned/Stale further weakens any durable-fix claim.
attacks.correct_version: Developer stated GRT finished after the two parameter changes. No quantitative post-change congestion/DRC data or end-to-end closure evidence is present; issue later auto-closed as stale.

attacks.claim: 20k routing congestion DRCs while placement density is only 0.24 with a lot of open space implies surprising failure
attacks.problem: Framing treats low average density as inherently protective. Global-route congestion can concentrate in channels around macros even when average density is low; the heatmap already localizes the problem to the macro and top-of-die region. No paradox is required.
attacks.correct_version: Placement density 0.24 left substantial open area, yet GRT still reported ~20 k congestion DRCs concentrated at the top of the die and around the macro.

attacks.problem: Inconsistent with the gaps the draft itself enumerates (missing post-fix metrics, no PR, unresolved #5971, stale closure).
